definition: A judicial opinion disagreeing with the majority; public disagreement in principle.
example: Dissents speak to a future age. It's not simply to say, 'My colleagues are wrong and I would do it this way,' but the greatest dissents do become court opinions.
source: Interviews on the role of dissent

definition: The state of being equal, especially in status, rights, and opportunities.
example: Women will only have true equality when men share with them the responsibility of bringing up the next generation.
source: Speeches on gender and law

definition: A person with full membership and standing under a constitution.
example: The pedestal upon which women have been placed has all too often, upon closer inspection, been a cage—and full citizenship means stepping off both.
source: Equal-protection advocacy

definition: A base supporting a statue; metaphorically, false elevation that restricts.
example: The pedestal upon which women have been placed has all too often, upon closer inspection, been a cage.
source: Equal-protection advocacy

definition: An enclosure that confines; a structure that looks protective but traps.
example: The pedestal upon which women have been placed has all too often, upon closer inspection, been a cage.
source: Equal-protection advocacy

definition: Preferential treatment; an unearned advantage.
example: I ask no favor for my sex. All I ask of our brethren is that they take their feet off our necks.
source: Quoting Sarah Grimké in advocacy and later remarks

definition: Fellow members of a group; here, men as co-citizens.
example: I ask no favor for my sex. All I ask of our brethren is that they take their feet off our necks.
source: Quoting Sarah Grimké in advocacy and later remarks

definition: The quality of being fair and reasonable under law.
example: Fight for the things that you care about, but do it in a way that will lead others to join you—that is how justice gains allies.
source: Advice to young people

definition: A person or group that cooperates with another for a common purpose.
example: Fight for the things that you care about, but do it in a way that will lead others to join you as an ally.
source: Advice to young people

definition: The fundamental principles and laws of a nation.
example: The Constitution is a living document to the extent that we read its grand principles in light of new understandings—without discarding its text.
source: Judicial philosophy remarks

definition: A formal statement of reasons for a judicial decision.
example: The greatest dissents do become court opinions and gradually over time their views become the dominant view.
source: On dissent

definition: The capacity to accept delay without anger while still pressing forward.
example: Real change, enduring change, happens one step at a time—and patience is not the enemy of urgency.
source: Reflections on reform

definition: Lasting over a long period; able to withstand strain.
example: Real change, enduring change, happens one step at a time.
source: Reflections on reform

definition: Relating to shared responsibility among colleagues; cooperative in tone.
example: You can disagree without being disagreeable—a collegial court still argues hard about the law.
source: On judicial culture

definition: Biological category of male or female; a basis of unjust legal classification.
example: I ask no favor for my sex. All I ask of our brethren is that they take their feet off our necks.
source: Quoting Sarah Grimké

definition: A single movement in a process of progress.
example: Real change, enduring change, happens one step at a time.
source: Reflections on reform

definition: Unpleasant to deal with; causing friction.
example: You can disagree without being disagreeable.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: Having the greatest influence.
example: The greatest dissents do become court opinions, and gradually over time their views become the dominant view.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: The theory and philosophy of law.
example: Her jurisprudence treated equality as a constitutional command, not a courtesy.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: An earlier decision treated as a guide for later ones.
example: A dissent today can be the precedent that a later court is finally ready to follow.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: A fixed, oversimplified picture of a group.
example: A stereotype written into law is still a stereotype, however politely it is drafted.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: To show to have been right, or to clear from blame.
example: She wrote to vindicate the Constitution's promise for people the majority had overlooked.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: Close, critical examination.
example: Laws that sort people by sex, she argued, must face real scrutiny, not a shrug.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: A legal sorting of people into groups that the law then treats differently.
example: Sex-based classification, she insisted, is not a favor. It is a limit dressed as protection.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: Belonging to, or allowed by, a constitution.
example: A constitutional principle that arrives late is still the law, and she was willing to wait it into view.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change

definition: A friend of the court who advises the judges without being a party to the case.
example: An amicus brief, in her career, was often how an outsider's life entered the record.
source: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
speech: On Dissent, Equality, and Enduring Change
